newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech opposition SocDems re-elect Zeman as leader.
newsitem.headline: Czech opposition SocDems re-elect Zeman as leader.

text.p: The leading Czech opposition party, the Social Democrats, re-elected Milos Zeman as their leader as expected on Saturday.

Zeman has held the post for four years, leading the CSSD from the opposition wilderness a surprisingly strong second place showing in general elections last spring, denying the centre-right government a parliamentary majority.

He has attempted at the party conference in this northeast Moravian town to re-unite the CSSD which has suffered from a huge rift after several deputies broke ranks in voting with the government on its 1997 balanced budget.
Earlier at the conference, the party expelled one of the deputies, Josef Wagner, chairman of the parliamentary budget committee, for his role in the vote.
A second deputy who voted against the wishes of the party, CSSD Vice-chairman Karel Machovec, is expected to lose his post at the conference which runs until Sunday.
Zeman has threatened that he will resign his chairmanship if the more centrist Machovec is re-elected to his position.
